suitability_reason: Section 72(t) additional tax: age 50 < 59 1/2; first-time homebuyer exception limited to individual retirement plans and distribution not shown to be from one; no equitable exception. 10% of $137,024 matches the $13,702 deficiency.

taxpayer.notes: Took retirement distributions totaling $137,024 to buy out brother's half of inherited Maryland house.

adjustments: 10% additional tax on early distributions under section 72(t)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Claims first-time homebuyer exception ($10,000) and that the 59 1/2 age rule and exceptions are arbitrary; CARES Act would have applied had he waited 30 days.
conceded: Respondent conceded the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty of $2,740

findings_of_fact.fact: Distributions of $45,921 (TIAACREF Brokerage) and $91,103 (TIAA Administrative Services LLC), total $137,024, reported as taxable income
findings_of_fact.snippet: received $45,921 and $91,103 from TIAACREF Brokerage and TIAA Administrative Services LLC, respectively, for a total of $137,024.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner was 50 years old in 2019 when distributions were made
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner was 50 years old in 2019 when the distributions were made.

findings_of_fact.fact: Property deeded from mother's estate to petitioner and brother as joint tenants on November 9, 2019; transferred to petitioner as sole owner for $130,000 on December 5, 2019
findings_of_fact.snippet: On December 5, 2019, the property was transferred to petitioner as the sole owner for the sum of $130,000.

findings_of_fact.fact: Forms 1099-R did not indicate the accounts were traditional, SEP or SIMPLE IRAs; no evidence that any part was from an individual retirement plan
findings_of_fact.snippet: The boxes were not checked on the Forms 1099

findings_of_fact.fact: Distributions made in 2019 (CARES Act relief applies to 2020 distributions)
findings_of_fact.snippet: had he made the distribution just 30 days later in 2020 instead of 2019, he would have qualified for the exception

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the 10% additional tax under section 72(t) on $137,024 of 2019 retirement distributions?
issues.holding: Yes. Under 59 1/2; first-time homebuyer exception applies only to individual retirement plans and petitioner did not show the distributions came from one; no equitable/hardship exception.
issues.computable_reason: Age 50 < 59 1/2; non-IRA source makes 72(t)(2)(F) unavailable; 10% x $137,024.

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent.
decision.summary: $13,702 section 72(t) deficiency sustained; 6662(a) penalty conceded by respondent.

notes: Some facts stipulated; record is stipulation plus petitioner's testimony. Petitioner testified to a 403(b) plan and partial Roth IRA source but produced no evidence. Respondent's alternative argument (prior ownership interest via 11/9/2019 deed under 72(t)(8)(D)(i)) not reached. Derived: 10% x $137,024 = $13,702.40, matching deficiency.
